intro: Cards, board games, bets and parties: the vocabulary of play.
p.baraja.consejo: The Spanish deck has forty cards and four suits: oros, copas, espadas and bastos.
p.barajar.consejo: It comes from «baraja». You also say «barajar posibilidades»: weighing several options.
p.repartir.consejo: With cards, you deal them at the start. It is regular: «reparto», «repartes». The noun is «el reparto».
p.partida.glosa: game (one round of cards or a board game)
p.partida.consejo: A «partido» is a sports match; a «partida» is of cards, chess or video games.
p.tablero.consejo: It comes from «tabla». The chessboard has sixty-four squares.
p.ficha.consejo: In parchís each player moves four counters. «Ficha» is also a card with data.
p.dado.consejo: It has six faces. You «tira el dado». «Dado» is also the participle of «dar».
p.turno.consejo: You respect the turn: first one, then another. At work there are morning or afternoon shifts.
p.tocarle a alguien.consejo: It works like «gustar»: «me toca», «te toca», «le toca». You ask: «¿A quién le toca?».
p.hacer trampas.consejo: You say «hacer trampa» or «hacer trampas». Whoever does it is a «tramposo».
p.apostar.consejo: The o becomes ue: «apuesto», «apuestas». «Te apuesto un helado a que gana».
p.lotería.consejo: The accent on the i separates the vowels: lo-te-RÍ-a. «Tocar la lotería» is to win it.
p.rompecabezas.consejo: It is the same in singular and plural: «un rompecabezas», «dos rompecabezas». Break + heads.
p.disfrazarse de.consejo: You say «disfrazarse de pirata». The noun is «el disfraz». It takes «se».
b1.texto:
**Three words.** A **juego** is the game in general: chess is a juego. A **partida** is one round of cards, chess or a video game. A «partido» is a sports match.

**Cards.** You **baraja** (shuffle), **reparte** (deal) and throw a card. The Spanish deck has forty cards.

**Board games.** On the **tablero** you move the **fichas** after throwing the **dado**. There are chess, draughts and parchís.

**Turns.** You say **tocarle a alguien**, like «gustar»: **¿A quién le toca? Me toca a mí.** It is also used for prizes: **le ha tocado la lotería**.

**Rules.** You must follow them. Whoever breaks them **hace trampas** (cheats) and is a «tramposo».

**Chance.** The **lotería** is a game of chance. **Apostar** is putting money on a result: **te apuesto un euro a que gana**.

**Fun.** A thousand-piece **rompecabezas**, a costume party, a night out. At a party you can **disfrazarse de** pirate. And at the end, the fireworks.
b2.titulo: A game of cards after dinner
b2.f0.texto: Shall we have a game of cards?
b2.f2.texto: Then I will deal seven cards to each of us.
b2.f4.texto: I bet you a euro that I win this game.
b2.f5.texto: Looking at other people's cards in the mirror is not allowed.
b2.f7.texto: If you had not hidden a card on Sunday, nobody would distrust you.
b4.texto:
To talk about something in the past that **did not happen**, use **si** + **hubiera** + participle, and in the other part the **conditional**: **Si hubieras barajado bien, no habríamos perdido.** The order can be changed: **No habríamos perdido si hubieras barajado bien.**

For something unreal in the present use **si** + imperfect subjunctive + conditional: **Si tuviera suerte, ganaría la lotería.**

The conditional is never put right after **si**.
b4.e0.texto: If you had shuffled well, we would not have lost.
b4.e1.texto: If I were lucky, I would win the lottery.
b4.e2.texto: We would have finished earlier if we had played without cheating.
b5.f0.texto: The rain taps on the windows of grandmother's house and muffles all the noises of the street.
b5.f1.texto: On the living-room table, an enormous puzzle shows half of a red lighthouse.
b5.f2.texto: The hot chocolate steams in the cups and fills the room with a sweet smell.
b5.f3.texto: With clumsy hands, the children shuffle the cards and deal them out on the tablecloth.
b5.f4.texto: Every time someone throws the dice, a small cry of joy runs through the house.
b5.f5.texto: At nightfall, grandmother opens the wardrobe and takes out a trunk full of old costumes.
b5.f6.texto: Daniel dresses up as a pirate with a red scarf and a cardboard sword.
b5.f7.texto: Nora prefers a blue dress with stars that shine in the light of the lamp.
b5.f8.texto: Afterwards everyone goes out onto the balcony and waits for the neighbourhood fireworks.
b5.f9.texto: A green light blooms in the wet sky and is reflected in the children's eyes.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: shuffling is mixing the cards before dealing them.
b6.o1.refuerzo: You throw the dice, not the cards, before starting.
b6.o2.refuerzo: You bet money or something else, not the cards.
b6.pregunta: What do you do with the cards before dealing them?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «tocarle a alguien» is in the third person: «te toca».
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Tocas» would be «tú tocas»; here the verb does not agree with «tú».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Tocan» is plural, but the turn is just one.
b7.pregunta: Which form of «tocar» completes the sentence?
b8.frase: La abuela reparte las cartas a todos
b8.traduccion: Grandmother deals the cards to everyone
b9.o0: Es mi turno de comprar un billete
b9.o0.refuerzo: Here «tocar» is not about turns but about a prize.
b9.o1: He ganado un premio de la lotería
b9.o1.refuerzo: Yes: with a prize, «tocar» means winning by luck.
b9.o2: He tocado un billete de lotería
b9.o2.refuerzo: It is not about touching with the hand, but about winning.
b9.pregunta: What does «Me ha tocado la lotería» mean?
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «the die» (a single dice).
b11.o0.refuerzo: An «a» is missing before it: you say «apostar a que».
b11.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «apostar a que» + verb is the correct form.
b12.o0.refuerzo: In chess you think each move; it does not depend on luck.
b12.o1.refuerzo: A puzzle needs thinking and looking at pieces, not luck.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes: in the lottery whoever is lucky wins.
b12.pregunta: Which is a game of chance?
p.echamos.consejo: «Echar una partida» means to have a game. Stress on CHA.
p.barajo.consejo: The j sounds like «h». The verb is about mixing cards.
p.gano.consejo: «Yo gano» is the first person of «ganar». Stress on GA.
p.trampas.consejo: «Hacer trampas» is to cheat. Feminine plural.
p.escondido.consejo: Participle with -ido. «Esconder» changes o to «ue» in the present.
p.desconfiaría.consejo: The -ía ending is the conditional. Stress on RI.
p.barajado.consejo: Past participle of «barajar». The j is strong, like «h».
p.hubiéramos.consejo: Used in conditional sentences: «si hubiéramos jugado».
p.jugado.consejo: With «haber», it forms the perfect: «hemos jugado».
p.humea.consejo: The h is silent. The e and a are separate: u-ME-a.
p.torpes.consejo: Plural of «torpe». The stress is on TOR.
p.barajan.consejo: Plural of «barajar». The j sounds like «h».
p.reparten.consejo: «Repartir» means to share out. Stress on PAR.
p.tira.consejo: «Tirar» means to throw or to pull. Stress on TI.
p.anochecer.consejo: «Al anochecer» means at dusk. The c before e sounds like «th».
p.saca.consejo: «Sacar» means to take out. The c before a sounds like «k».
p.baúl.consejo: The accent on ú separates the vowels: ba-UL.
p.disfraza.consejo: «Disfrazarse de» means to dress up as.
p.pirata.consejo: Used for men and women: «el pirata», «la pirata».
p.pañuelo.consejo: The ñ sounds like «ny». The stress is on NYWE.
p.espada.consejo: Feminine, but starts with «a» stressed, so it is «la espada».
p.salen.consejo: «Salir» is to go out. Stress on SA.
p.florece.consejo: «Florecer» is to bloom. Also used for things that appear and spread.
p.reparte.consejo: Third person of «repartir». Stress on PAR.
